# Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-315#speed-up-provider-rate-limit-checks

**Verdict: Caught** (limited to the page case's owner-held path).

**Story and revision.** `.planning/seeds/SEED-315-provider-rate-limit-checks.md#speed-up-provider-rate-limit-checks`, plan `.planning/slice-plans/598-speed-up-provider-rate-limit-checks/PLAN.md`, completed implementation revision `449a0b919889ea357dca764eb73075b7485fdf31` (the checkout's HEAD `cc45c8907` adds only a plan record over it).

**Promise.** "Owner time held before the directed time while page time passes it: the owner refuses the read and GitHub is asked nothing. The admission under proof is the owner's, not the page's schedule." Expected observable behavior: the check the page makes at its own directed time is answered 502 by the read boundary with the whole two seconds still left, and no `gh` call reaches GitHub.

**Fault.** The caller's suggested fault direction was kept: the released owner admits a read before the directed time. Location `src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/github-request-admission.mjs`, `ReadAdmission.heldBack`: `return nowMs < this.#resumesAtMs ? {held-back…} : undefined` changed to `return false && nowMs < this.#resumesAtMs ? … : undefined`, so the owner never refuses during a standing wait. One edit; fixtures and assertions untouched.

**Fixtures.** `dashboard/tests/support/ownerClockTest.ts` and `dashboard/tests/support/listingReuseWithOwnerClock.ts` (the released owner in its own process with a test-advanced `Date`), unchanged.

**Maintained checks examined.** The caller's focused command was reused unchanged, at one worker, in a scratch worktree: `npm run --silent test:dashboard -- --workers=1 --reporter=list --grep 'auto refresh rate limit: a rate-limited check waits|a rate-limited stream answer shows'` (Homebrew bash first on PATH; `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` unset). It selects `dashboard/tests/observation/auto-refresh-rate-limit.spec.ts:75` and the rate-limited case at `dashboard/tests/observation/revision-stream-lost.spec.ts:91`.

**Run observations.**
- Baseline (unfaulted, scratch at `449a0b919`, `git status --short` empty): 2 passed, both cases executed (page case 13.3 s, stream case 5.9 s; run 56.0 s).
- Wrong behavior, observed independently of the tests: a scratch script (`ic-witness.mjs`) imports the scratch `ReadAdmission`, records a 429 directing two seconds at time T, and asks `heldBack(T+1000)`. Unfaulted: `{"kind":"held-back","waitSeconds":1}`. Faulted: `ADMITTED`. So the fault makes the owner admit a read before the directed time.
- Faulted run: 1 failed, 1 passed (14.2 s). The page case failed inside the step "owner time held before the directed time, the check page time reaches is refused by the owner and asks GitHub nothing", at the helper `passTimeUntilLimited`, `expect(response.status()).toBe(502)` (`auto-refresh-rate-limit.spec.ts:68`, called from line 133): expected 502, received 200. Reach: the two earlier steps passed, so the first limit was recorded and the page kept its own schedule; the failing check is the one page time reached while owner time stood still, and it was answered instead of refused. The catch is this earlier helper assertion; the step's own later assertions (`held.retryAfterSeconds` 2, the "was not asked of GitHub" text, `callsSince(page, quietFrom)` equal to `[]`) were not reached.
- The stream case passed under the same fault (2.2 s). In this run it did not discriminate an owner that never holds: nothing in it asks during the wait except on the page's own schedule. This is an observation about that one case under this one fault, not a verdict on it.
- Restoration: the original file was copied back and compared byte-identical (`cmp`), scratch `git status --short` empty as before the probe, witness again reports `held-back`, and the same command reran 2 passed (page case 4.7 s, stream case 2.3 s; run 12.0 s). The scratch worktree (`/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/167b7876/tmp/ic-scratch`) was then removed; the supplied checkout was never edited.
- Full unfiltered logs: `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/167b7876/tmp/ic-baseline.log`, `ic-fault.log`, `ic-restored.log`; witness `ic-witness.mjs` in the same directory.

**Next proof action.** None is required for the selected promise on the page path: maintained proof exercises the owner admitting early and fails on it. Separately from the verdict, if the stream case is meant to prove the owner's hold rather than the page's schedule, the missing observation is a stream-path read attempted while owner time is held before the directed time; this probe did not establish whether such a transition exists there, so that would need its own check.

**Prior disposition.** The execution's earlier scratch observations (removing each case's owner advance fails the case) covered the fixture-binding direction; this probe adds the product/owner direction the caller noted as untried. No new repair decision arises from this probe; test repair and follow-up routing stay with the caller.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** 82.2 s (measured), sum of the Playwright runner's reported run durations for the three focused runs: baseline 56.0 s, faulted 14.2 s, restored 12.0 s. Host load average was about 17 at the baseline.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part in the probe and no measure of the requester's time was observed.
- **Agent effort.** 10 tool operations (measured, counted from this invocation's tool calls up to and including the report finisher); token usage unavailable, since the agent cannot read its own usage.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 186047 ms (measured), from 1794457748548 to 1794457934595 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.


---

## Wrap-up disposition

- **Checked revision:** `449a0b919889ea357dca764eb73075b7485fdf31`.
- **Evidence:** the report above; logs `ic-baseline.log`, `ic-fault.log` and `ic-restored.log` of the probe.
- **Decision:** Caught; no follow-up is queued. The probe names no actionable finding for the selected promise. Its side observation that the rate-limited stream case passed with an owner that never holds is not a gap in a story promise: that case promises that the stream closes, stays closed until the directed time on the page's schedule and reopens with a full freshness bound, and it fails without its owner-time advance at the catch-up to B, as the execution observed. The owner's refusal itself is the page case's promise, which the probe caught.
- **Canonical follow-up links:** none.
